fin_derrota_vida_txt: Without biodiversity, the planet stopped holding itself together.
fin_derrota_esperanza_txt: Without people who believe, there is no transition.
fin_derrota_tiempo_txt: 2150 arrived and the climate wasn't reversed.

ayuda_txt: Each turn is a year. Tap a tile, build a Project Drawdown solution and upgrade it. Solutions cost ⚡ and ⛏, which refill every year up to a cap: what you don't spend is lost. Look after Life and Hope: if either hits 0, you lose. Beware of traps: they're cheap and seem to work… until they're exposed. You win when temperature falls ten years in a row with net-negative emissions.
evita: Avoids up to {g} Gt a year
captura: Removes up to {g} Gt a year
evita_sup: Avoids up to {g} Gt a year
g_hola: Hi! I'm Ceiba. I'm named after the sacred tree of many peoples of the Americas, the one that joins earth and sky. I'll show you how this works, one bit at a time. The idea is simple: cool the planet down, using solutions that already exist.
g_temp: This matters most: Earth is already 1.5 °C warmer than before the Industrial Revolution. In 2024 we crossed that line for the first time. Every tenth of a degree brings more fires, droughts and hurricanes.
g_emis: Why is it warming? Because of the greenhouse gases (GHG) we release: CO₂, methane, nitrous oxide. They trap heat like a blanket. Today we release 57 gigatonnes (Gt) a year, that is, 57 billion tonnes. As long as that number is above zero, the planet keeps warming.
g_meta: Here's your world's history: the orange line is temperature, the teal one is emissions. You win when temperature falls 10 years in a row with emissions below zero, meaning you remove more carbon than you release.
g_barras: Cutting GHG isn't enough. Look after Life (biodiversity: forests, reefs, animals) and Hope (the people pushing for change). If either hits zero, you lose. You also lose if the planet passes 3 °C.
g_tocar: Let's start with a city. The blinking tiles are cities: tap one. I've turned Bogotá towards you.
g_cajon: Each card is a real solution, measured by Project Drawdown, a group of scientists who calculated how much each one can cut the world's emissions. The green number is the most it would avoid if the whole planet adopted it. Tap a card's i and I'll tell you more. Pick one and build it.
g_recursos: Building costs energy and materials. They refill every year and have a cap: what you don't spend is lost. Every terrain gives something, like in Catan: forests and crops give materials; deserts, grasslands and sea give energy. If you have too much of one, swap it with the arrows button.
g_siguiente: Each turn is a year. When you can't afford anything else, end the year and see what happened.
g_despues: Read the card: it tells you how emissions and temperature changed, and what happened around the world.
g_mejorar: Solutions start slow and speed up as your world adopts them. Tap one of your buildings to upgrade it (up to level 5): it does more and its terrain produces more. Careful: not everything that glitters works. And look at the sky: animals are migrating. Tap them.
g_a_trampa: Something ugly came out: that solution didn't work as promised. Project Drawdown doesn't recommend it. Its real effect was tiny, it harms Life, and people felt fooled: that's why Hope dropped. You can demolish it: tap the building with the red sign.
g_a_era2: New solutions unlocked: solar farms, offshore wind, ecosystem restoration and more. Restoration doesn't just avoid emissions: it pulls CO₂ out of the air. You'll need it to get below zero.
g_a_evento: A disaster knocked down some buildings. More heat brings more events. Life softens them, and mangroves and salt marshes protect their coasts.
g_a_inflexion: You crossed a tipping point: a change on Earth that doesn't come back, like thawing permafrost. It releases emissions you can't switch off. Better not cross the next ones.
g_a_esperanza: Hope is falling. It rises when people see results (emissions or temperature going down) and with people-centred solutions: transit, bikes, food, compost. It drops with disasters, exposed traps and investing in only a few regions. Big policies are paid with Hope.
g_a_vida: Life is in danger. It rises by protecting and restoring ecosystems: forests, peatlands, mangroves, seagrass. Heat, background deforestation and traps drain it.
g_a_negativas: Emissions below zero! Your world now removes more than it releases. Fact: the real world removes about 2.2 Gt a year, and 99.9% of it is done by forests (The State of CDR, 2026).
g_a_racha: Temperature has been falling for a few years. Keep it up for 10 in a row and you reverse climate change.
g_a_recursos: You have spare energy and the cap will eat it. Spend it, or swap it for materials with the arrows button.
tip_temp: Temperature: how much warmer your planet is than before industry (1850-1900). Today: 1.5 °C. At 3 °C you lose.
tip_emis: Net emissions: the greenhouse gases your world releases in a year, minus what it removes, in gigatonnes (billions of tonnes) of CO₂ equivalent. Get them below zero.
tip_ener: Energy: refills every year. Solar, wind, efficiency (every LED frees energy) and desert, grassland and sea terrain give it. It has a cap.
tip_mat: Materials: refill every year. Recycling, compost and forest, crop and mountain terrain give them. They have a cap.
tip_vida: Life: biodiversity. It rises by protecting and restoring ecosystems; it falls with heat, deforestation and traps. More Life means nature removes more CO₂ and disasters hit softer. At 0 you lose.
tip_esp: Hope: the people pushing for change. It rises when they see results and with people-centred solutions; it falls with disasters, injustice and exposed traps. High Hope makes everything cheaper and pays for policies. At 0 you lose.
gl_drawdown_txt: A nonprofit that reviewed hundreds of climate solutions and calculated how much each one can reduce emissions. The game's 166 solutions come from its Drawdown Explorer (2025). Some are rated not recommended: in the game they're traps.
gl_gt_txt: Gigatonnes of CO₂ equivalent per year. A gigatonne is a billion tonnes. "Equivalent" because methane and other gases are counted as the CO₂ that would warm the same. Today the world emits about 57 Gt a year (UNEP, 2024).
gl_temp_txt: Warming above pre-industrial times. It follows all the CO₂ ever accumulated: while we emit, it rises; if we emit below zero, it falls slowly. Methane warms hard but doesn't last, so cutting it cools fast.
gl_netas_txt: When you remove more CO₂ than you release: restoring forests, peatlands, mangroves, or with technology. It's the only way temperature goes down.
gl_adopcion_txt: How much of a solution's potential the world already uses. It grows in an S-curve: slow, then fast, then full. Upgrading a solution pushes it.
gl_trampas_txt: Solutions Project Drawdown doesn't recommend: carbon capture on coal plants, corn ethanol, ocean fertilization... They look cheap and fast. Later it turns out their effect was tiny and they harm Life.
gl_politicas_txt: Big decisions, like closing coal plants, paid with Hope. They cut a whole sector's emissions at once.
gl_inflexion_txt: Parts of Earth that change for good past a certain heat: permafrost, corals, the Amazon (Armstrong McKay et al., 2022).

c_bosque: Forests and jungles: protect and restore them. They give materials.
c_cultivo: Crops and grasslands: food, biochar, silvopasture.
c_desierto: Deserts: solar farms. They give lots of energy.
c_mar: Coastal sea and ocean: seaweed, seagrass, offshore wind.
c_costa: Coasts: mangroves. They give you a port for swapping resources.
c_seco: If a tile looks brown, it's degraded or drying out from the heat.
h_meta_txt: You win when temperature falls 10 years in a row with net emissions below zero. You lose if Life or Hope hit 0, or if you pass 3 °C.
h_turno_txt: Tap a tile, build a solution, upgrade it, and end the year. At the end of the year you see what happened.
h_recursos_txt: They refill every year with a base amount plus what your buildings and their terrain produce. They have a cap: spend them. If you have too much of one, swap 3 for 1 (2 for 1 with a port).
h_vida_txt: Rises with nature solutions (protect and restore). Falls with heat, deforestation and traps. More Life means nature removes more CO₂ and disasters hit softer.
h_esp_txt: Rises when emissions or temperature fall and with people-centred solutions (transit, food, compost). Falls with disasters, unfair investment and exposed traps. It makes everything cheaper and pays for policies.
h_trampas_txt: Some solutions promise a lot and cost little. Read each card's i before building: Ceiba tells you what the science says.
h_politicas_txt: Big decisions, like closing coal plants, paid with Hope. They cut a whole sector's emissions at once.
h_gt_txt: Greenhouse gases (GHG) trap heat. They're measured in gigatonnes (Gt) of CO₂ equivalent: a billion tonnes. Today the world releases 57 a year (UNEP, 2024).
h_drawdown_txt: A nonprofit that assessed hundreds of climate solutions and calculated how much each one can reduce. The game's come from its Drawdown Explorer (2025).
